articles.title: Scotland hold off late Australia rally to secure narrow victory
articles.summary: Scotland 15-12 Australia. Fagerson and Dempsey touch down in Murrayfiield. After the pyrotechnics in Paris on Friday and a wondrous Welsh win in Cardiff on Saturday, this was a much more prosaic affair.
body: Scotland could not afford another patchy performance like last weekend, when they excelled in the first half against New Zealand before capitulating in the second. They edged over the line at a sodden Murrayfield, but might have fallen to a calamitous defeat had Darcy Graham not foiled a last-minute attack by the Wallabies.

The home team won the arm-wrestle – just – but the limitations of this Australia side are well known, and the visitors would have hoped for anything but the heavy rain they encountered. They have lost four in a row under Les Kiss and will go to Wales even more desperate for a win.

Scotland leapfrog Wales, conquerors of the mighty All Blacks, to move fourth in the northern hemisphere table on points difference. In the context of their campaign this was a pivotal occasion with two wins and two losses on the ledger. A knee injury to the captain, Sione Tuipulotu, prompted a late reshuffle by Townsend: Bristol’s Tom Jordan started at No 12, with the openside flanker Rory Darge taking the armband.

articles.title: Emotional Rory McIlroy dedicates record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title to father
articles.summary: McIlroy’s father, Gerry, is recovering after major surgery. ‘He said: “Go and win the Race to Dubai.” This is for him’ An emotional Rory McIlroy dedicated a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title to his father, Gerry, who is recovering from major surgery in the United States.
body: McIlroy’s final round of 67 at the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai helped him to finish in second place, which was sufficient to edge out Eugenio Chacarra for the season-long order of merit crown. Tyrrell Hatton won the tournament itself, with Chacarra’s share of third meaning McIlroy prevailed by the narrow margin of 125 points. He later revealed Gerry had been at the forefront of his mind.
“He has been in hospital for the last two months,” McIlroy said. “He underwent a huge operation at the end of September and he is recovering well thankfully.
“When I was coming to the Middle East, I went up to Cleveland to see him before I went and he said to me: ‘Go and win the Race to Dubai.’ This one is for him.”

McIlroy’s parents have been regular attendees at events throughout his golfing journey. When reflecting on his highlight of 2026, McIlroy said being able to play at Augusta National with his father in the lead up to the Masters meant more to him than claiming a second Green Jacket.

articles.title: NFL: Lions thump Patriots in Munich on St Brown's German homecoming
articles.summary: Jahmyr Gibbs was unstoppable and Amon-Ra St Brown starred on his German homecoming as the Detroit Lions torched the Drake Maye-less New England Patriots 35-10 at the Allianz Arena in Munich on Sunday.
body: Gibbs finished with 252 yards and two touchdowns from scrimmage, including 153 rushing yards and 99 through the air, while St Brown - born to a German mother - recorded four catches for 98 yards and two scores to reward his hero's welcome in Europe.
New England's offense capitulated after the opening drive of the game when Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury before being replaced by Tommy DeVito at quarterback.

DeVito struggled to move the ball as he finished 12 of 24 for 81 yards, one touchdown and one interception while being sacked four times. Lions quarterback Jared Goff was 20 of 31 for 303 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions.
It marked the penultimate game of a record nine international matchups in 2026 as the league prepares to conclude its road-trip in Mexico City next Sunday.

articles.title: Record-breaking Andy Robertson is Scotland’s finest captain
articles.summary: As he passes Kenny Dalglish’s appearance total, it is important to remember that it is the left-back’s journey that sets him apart. Andy Robertson may not be Scotland’s greatest player, but he is indisputably their finest captain.
body: There is no requirement to compare a left-back in 2026 to a forward from decades earlier. Dalglish and Robertson are men in different positions in essentially a different sport. Instead, Robertson’s march to the top of the cap pile gives cause to laud his contribution.

Those within the Scotland setup regard Robertson as the glue who holds the scene together, a decorated footballer who treats everybody the same and carries out an abundance of unseen work to make this team better. Robertson has routinely paid for squad nights from his own pocket.

The 32-year-old is as dedicated to overall environment as he is to his craft. Under Robertson’s on-field guidance, Scotland have morphed from international also-rans to serial tournament participants.

Left-backs are rarely the recipients of praise. When of the status of Robertson they do, however, receive criticism when a team struggle. He has carried the heaviest load while probably unable to celebrate the highs in an appropriate manner.

Andy Robertson may not be Scotland’s greatest player, but he is indisputably their finest captain.
There is no requirement to compare a left-back in 2026 to a forward from decades earlier.
Dalglish and Robertson are men in different positions in essentially a different sport.

articles.title: Fisher wants fight with AJ dangerman Prenga early next year
articles.summary: Johnny Fisher is looking to return to action early in 2027 and wants to fight Kristian Prenga, the man who almost derailed the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua mega-fight.
body: In July, Prenga boxed Joshua in what was meant to be a tune-up fight for the former world champion. Instead Prenga put him down heavily twice in their first round. He was on the edge of victory only for Joshua to storm back and knock him out in the second round.
Prenga caught the eye of the boxing world in that fight and Fisher would like the man who almost beat Joshua to be his next opponent.

"Prenga would be good. That's a good sort of stepping stone to where I want to be. Someone who's fought one of the best heavyweights we've had in Great Britain in recent years, or in memory in general," Fisher told Sky Sports.
"So to be in the ring with someone like that, who carries knockout power, carries the ability to drop people, like Anthony Joshua, at the top of the division - so let's see what I can do."

articles.title: Chapecoense crash survivor wins promotion in final game
articles.summary: Alan Ruschel, one of six survivors in the 2016 plane crash that was carrying members of the Chapecoense team, wins promotion to Brazil‘s Serie A in his final match before retiring.
body: Alan Ruschel, a survivor of the 2016 plane crash that was carrying the Chapecoense football team, won promotion to Brazil's Serie A in his final game before retirement.
Ruschel, 37, was one of just six survivors when the plane crashed in Colombia and killed 71 people, including 19 of the club's players and the coaching staff.

Despite severe injuries and spinal surgery, Ruschel returned to football a year later and retires after earning promotion to Brazil's top flight with Juventude, his boyhood club which he re-joined in 2023.
Ruschel came off the bench in the 74th minute to help see out a 2-0 win over Botafogo, resulting in an emotional farewell with a lap of honour at the club's Alfredo Jaconi Stadium.

articles.title: Zverev begins ATP Finals with straight-sets victory over Jodar
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev began his ATP Finals campaign with a 6-4 6-4 victory over rising star Rafael Jodar, who was competing in the event for the first time.
body: Zverev claimed his first two Grand Slam titles this year and became world No 1 for the first time too.
He is aiming for his third ATP Finals trophy after taking the season-ending event in 2018 and 2021.
"It's been a very good year for me. A lot of things that I've wanted to achieve I have achieved this year," Zverev said. "But playing here you can never take it for granted."
The 20-year-old Jodar is the first man to qualify for the Finals in the same season as his tour-level debut.

articles.title: Pioneer Pete sparks jubilant Greatwood scenes at Cheltenham
articles.summary: Pioneer Pete could have the County Hurdle back at Cheltenham in March as a target after continuing his charge up the two-mile hurdling rankings in the Unibet Greatwood Handicap Hurdle.
body: Posting a fourth win on the spin and backing up his impressive Welsh Champion Hurdle win at Chepstow, the likeable five-year-old was always in the front rank under Jonjo O'Neill Jnr and came clear to win by six and a half lengths at 7-2 from Tennessee Tango.

Victory for O'Neill, winning on the horse for the fifth time and riding for his father-brother training combination of Jonjo and AJ O'Neill, put welcome gloss on a day in which he had fallen twice from three previous rides.

"I thought Chepstow was his limit, but he is an amazing little horse," said O'Neill senior. "I have no idea how much more is left in the locker, but he is a horse in form and you would have to look at all those options like the County Hurdle now."
The training duo landed the County Hurdle with Wilful last March and AJ O'Neill admitted they are hoping the five-year-old may be good enough to chart a similar path.

articles.title: Why Northern Ireland won't focus on point they need in Hungary
articles.summary: A draw in Hungary on Tuesday would secure Nations League promotion for Northern Ireland, but they are targeting all three points in Budapest.
body: Still the only side in the 2026-27 Nations League yet to concede a goal, Northern Ireland know that one more clean sheet will be enough to secure back-to-back promotions.

After Saturday's 1-0 victory over Ukraine in Belfast, a draw away to Hungary in Budapest on Tuesday night would ensure Michael O'Neill's team top their group and advance to League A for the first time.

With three wins and two draws from their five games played, the visitors to the Puskas Arena are in the box seat in Group B2, but they will travel targeting victory rather than the draw that would suffice.
"We try and win every single game. If you don't, there's no point going," said veteran striker Josh Magennis, who will win a 94th cap should he feature.

articles.title: Rory McIlroy’s Tearful Dubai Win Is Pure Heart Over Stats
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy secured his eighth Race to Dubai title on Sunday with a bogey-free 67, but the real victory was his emotional tribute to his father. The Northern Irishman finished second at the DP World Tour Championship, yet he claimed the season-long crown by just 125 points over Eugenio Chacarra.
body: The Northern Irishman fought back tears while speaking to the press after the final round. He revealed that his father, Gerry, has been hospitalized for two months following a major surgery. “He underwent a huge operation at the end of September and is recovering well, thankfully,” a tearful McIlroy said, according to ESPN. The golfer traveled to Cleveland to visit his father before heading to the Middle East, where he received a direct instruction to win the title. “When I left to come to the Middle East, I went up to Cleveland to see him and he said to me, ‘Go win the Race to Dubai.’ This one’s for him,” he explained, according to ESPN.

Matching Montgomerie’s eight Order of Merit titles is a massive achievement, yet McIlroy insists this specific record was never his main goal. He grew up watching the Scottish legend play and admired his consistency, but he did not set out to equal the number of trophies. “Winning eight Order of Merits was never really in my list of goals when I was growing up,” McIlroy said, according to Golfmagic. The focus shifted entirely to his family during the tense final round, where he and Chacarra swapped the top spot in the standings multiple times.

articles.title: A fairytale ending! Chapecoense plane crash survivor Alan Ruschel wins promotion to Brazil's Serie A in final game before retirement
articles.summary: Alan Ruschel has officially hung up his boots, bringing the curtain down on one of the most emotional and inspiring careers in world football. The veteran defender, who miraculously survived the 2016 Chapecoense air disaster, secured a dream farewell by helping boyhood club Juventude clinch…
body: In a scene straight out of a Hollywood script, Ruschel finished his professional journey on the highest possible note, sealing promotion to Brazil's top flight with his boyhood club Juventude - whom he re-joined in 2023. It marks a remarkable final chapter for the 37-year-old, who was one of just six survivors of the 2016 plane crash in Colombia that claimed 71 lives, including 19 Chapecoense players and the coaching staff, before defying severe injuries and spinal surgery to return to the pitch a year later.

Reflecting on his deep connection with the club, the veteran was quick to point out the symmetry of his career path. 'I arrived here in 2007 with the club in Serie A and I am leaving the club there as well,' Ruschel told a Brazilian television station following the final whistle.

articles.title: Where is Ohio State football ranked in Coaches poll after Week 11?
articles.summary: Ohio State football (7-3) took a slight step up in the Week 11 US LBM Coaches Poll. The Buckeyes won their first game in nearly a month, defeating Northwestern 28-19 on Nov. 14 at Ohio Stadium. Ohio State was on a two-game losing streak after falling to USC 30-18 and Oregon 41-28.
body: As a result of the two losses, the Buckeyes dropped from No. 2 to No. 20 in the coaches poll. Ohio State went into the season ranked the No. 1 team by both the media and coaches.

Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith added the all-time Big Ten receiving yards record to his resume in the first half against Northwestern. Finishing the game with 3,874 career receiving yards, surpassing Prudue's John Standeford record of 3,788, which he set in 2003.
Freshman Luke Fahey went 21 for 32, logging 201 passing yards, three touchdowns and an interception during his first win for Ohio State.
